_judged_rubric.ph: 1 = measured lake pH of 9 or more (alkaline water of the kind that deposits carbonates). 0.5 = measured between 8.5 and 9, or described as soda or alkaline without a measurement, or measurements that straddle 9 or conflict. Left out when unknown. Jezero's ancient lake has no measured pH, so this compares with the conditions inferred from its carbonates, not with a Mars measurement.
_judged_rubric.minerals: 1 = magnesium-bearing carbonate deposits (hydromagnesite, magnesite, huntite) like those NASA compares with Jezero. 0.5 = other carbonate deposits (calcite, aragonite, dolomite, travertine). Left out when unknown.
_judged_rubric.water: 1 = closed-basin lake that concentrates by evaporation. 0.5 = lake with an outflow, through-flow or a link to the sea. Left out when unknown.
_judged_rubric.sediments: 1 = microbialites, delta or layered lake deposits documented. 0.5 = microbial mats or carbonate muds without documented microbialite structures. Left out when unknown.

_source_check: Each judged entry has 'checked': how the AI saw the source. 'read directly' means the source text itself was opened and supports the entry. 'source opened ... entry not confirmed' means the source was opened and does not support all of the entry. Anything else still needs a person to open the source.
_candidate_changes: 2026-11-14: at the team's request, 111 lakes in Türkiye with no published evidence entered and more than 150 km from Lake Salda were removed, and 24 lakes from other countries were added (carbonate and microbialite lakes, impact-crater lakes, soda lakes, and well-known large lakes as expected poor analogs). Removing and adding places changes the spread of each measured variable, so every score shifts a little.
